The input and send button live inside the body of a tab bar, using gpui-kit's default tab styling. There is a tab for each of the [PromptModesScope](../modes/index.md#prompt-modes-scope), in their order: Code, Chain, Spec, and Ask. Code, Spec, and Ask are ordinary tabs. Chain is also a tab, just a small one, because it only shows an icon. All four sit flush against each other with no extra gaps, and no tab has more padding than a normal tab.
The chat input starts in the combined mode: Chain is selected, so Code and Spec are selected together, and a prompt sent before switching tabs changes the code and the spec together.
Pressing <Ctrl+Tab> while in the chat input cycles from Code to Chain to Spec to Ask and back to Code, <Ctrl+Shift+Tab> the other way, and focus remains in the chat input. It is <Ctrl> on macOS too, not <Cmd>.
<Tab> and <Shift+Tab> don't switch tabs, and don't indent the text

###### Either

they move keyboard focus out of the chat input to the next

or previous control, as they do everywhere else. While the completion menu is open, <Tab> is still the menu's.

##### Chain

Chain is a tab with unusual behaviour. It shows an icon rather than a label, reading "Code and Spec" as its tooltip, and selecting it selects both Code and Spec. It never shows a focus outline, and its icon looks evenly spaced between Code and Spec whichever of the two is selected.
Unselected, it shows a broken chain dimmed to 50% opacity, and sits between Code and Spec like any other tab, overlapping neither of them.
In combined mode, with Chain selected, Chain has no line along its bottom, just as the joined Code and Spec beneath it have none. In separate mode, unselected, it has one, like any other unselected

###### Tab

the tab bar's bottom line runs beneath it, the same colour and

thickness, in the same place, as beneath any other unselected tab, at any display scale. This holds at every window size and display scale, in light and dark mode: in combined mode nothing draws a line beneath Chain at all, rather than a line being drawn and then hidden, since a hidden line can show again wherever rounding to the display's pixels uncovers it.
Selected, it shows a joined chain at full opacity. Selecting it animates as though it took a margin of -50% of its own width on both its left and right sides: Code and Spec slide together until they meet underneath it, so it ends up sitting on top of both. Deselecting it animates them apart again. While Chain is selected, Code and Spec both show as selected and read as a single unified tab, with no line between them. Chain itself has a transparent background and no left or right borders, so the joined Code and Spec show through underneath it.

##### Help

To the right of the tabs, filling the rest of the bar, a line of help text says what the selected tab is for, and changes as soon as another tab is selected. It is extra small and dimmer than muted text, set a little apart from the last tab, so it reads as a quiet note about the tab rather than as another tab. It is cut off rather than wrapped when the bar is too narrow.
It reads what the selected tab's mode is for, as the [PromptModesScope](../modes/index.md#prompt-modes-scope) says.

##### Session

At the far right of the bar, at the right end of the help text, sits how much context the selected tab's conversation holds, then a New conversation button. The questions of the Ask tab have a conversation of their own, and the other tabs share the tasks', as the [HarnessIntegrationScope](../../harness-integration/index.md#harness-integration-scope) says, so the figure is the Ask tab's conversation while it is selected, and the tasks' on any other tab.
The figure reads "Context", then the number of tokens, short and extra small, muted: "850", "42.1k", "123k", or "1.2M", to a decimal place below a hundred of a unit. It follows each reply as the harness reports it. While the next prompt would start a new conversation, as when the project has none yet or New conversation was just pressed, it reads "Context 0". Its tooltip says how many tokens the conversation the next prompt carries on holds, or that the next prompt starts a new conversation.
New conversation is a small ghost button with a sparkles icon, reading "New conversation". Pressing it starts a new conversation for the selected tab: the tasks' on Code, Chain, and Spec, the questions' on Ask. The next run in that tab, or in any tab sharing its conversation, starts a new one with no context instead of carrying on, and the figure reads "Context 0". A run of the conversation left that is still going finishes as it would, but neither it nor the project's history brings that conversation back, even once the project is closed and opened again, as the [HarnessIntegrationScope](../../harness-integration/index.md#harness-integration-scope) says.
It can be pressed while a run in that conversation is under way, a task on Code, Chain, or Spec, or any question on Ask, without waiting for it to finish. Pressed while a task runs, the prompts sent meanwhile queue as ever, and the next task to run from the queue, the first in it, starts a new conversation with no context, the ones after it carrying that one on. That holds even when the running task is the first of its conversation and the harness hasn't yet said which conversation it is: once it does, it isn't carried on either.
Its tooltip says which conversation it resets: "Start a new conversation for tasks" or "Start a new conversation for questions", adding, while a run in it is under way, that the run finishes in the conversation left. It is disabled only while that conversation has nothing to carry on and no run in it is under way, its tooltip then saying the next task, or question, already starts a new conversation.
Both sit on the bar's bottom line, which runs beneath them as it does beneath the help text, and neither is cut off: the help text gives way to them when the bar is narrow.

##### Usage

Just right of the context figure, before New conversation, sits the agent's usage: how much of the harness picked, of the [HarnessIntegrationScope](../../harness-integration/index.md#harness-integration-scope), has been used, as Claude Code's /usage shows it. Its summary is short and extra small, muted like the context figure: "Usage", then the share used of the plan limit nearest to running out, such as "Usage 42%", turning the theme's warning colour from 80% and its error colour once the limit is reached. When the harness reports no plan limits, the summary is the cost of this project's runs since it was opened, such as "Usage $1.24", or the tokens they used, as the context figure is written, when it reports no cost either. Until anything has been reported, it reads "Usage", with nothing after it.
Clicking the summary opens a popover above it with all the details, each group headed, and each figure labelled:
- Plan limits: each limit the harness reports, such as the current
  session's and the week's, with the share used as a bar and a
  percentage, and when it resets.
- Conversation: the context the selected tab's conversation holds,
  and its input, output, cache-read, and cache-written tokens, and
  its cost.
- This project: the same totals for every run in the project since
  it was opened, tasks and questions, and how many runs there were.
- The harness and model the figures came from, and when they were
  last reported.
A group, or a figure, the harness doesn't report is left out rather than shown as zero, and when nothing has been reported the popover says so. The figures come from what the harness reports as its runs go, never from running anything of its own to ask, and update in place while the popover is open, following each reply. Clicking outside the popover, or pressing Escape, closes it. The summary's tooltip says to click for the details. Like the context figure, it is never cut off: the help text gives way to it.

##### Slice

Just left of the context figure sits the Slice toggle: a small ghost button with a scissors icon, reading "Slice", which shows as selected while it is on. It starts off. Its tooltip says what the prompt is sent as: while off, the prompt written as a spec, its references linking to the spec they name; while on, the prompt with the `piton slice` of each spec it references. Clicking it turns it on or off, and it applies to every tab, Ask included. It stays as it is across sends, tab switches, and project switches, as the prompt being written does, and the help text gives way to it as it does to the session controls.

##### Colour

The selected tab and the tab body holding the input are tinted the colour of its mode, of the [PromptModesScope](../modes/index.md#prompt-modes-scope). With Chain selected, Code, Spec, and the body are all purple. The colour transitions smoothly whenever the selected tab changes, straight from the old tab's colour to the new one's. The tabs wrap around, so pressing <Ctrl+Tab> on Ask fades green straight to Code's red, and <Ctrl+Shift+Tab> on Code fades red straight to Ask's green; neither lights up Chain or Spec on the way.
The send button, both its halves, takes the same colour as the selected tab, purple with Chain selected, but at full strength rather than as a tint, so it stands out against the tinted body. Its label and chevron are in the theme's text colour for a solid hue, and the line between its halves is only faintly darker or lighter than it, half as far as its hover, just enough to part them. Disabled, the button fades as a disabled button does, in the same colour, and the line fades with the half it borders, never staying solid across a faded button.

#### System Prompt

The selected tab is the mode a prompt is sent in, and each mode's system prompt is sent with it, as the [ModeSystemPromptsScope](../mode-system-prompts/index.md#mode-system-prompts-scope) says.

#### Ask

Ask is for simply asking a question, which runs as the [PromptModesScope](../modes/index.md#prompt-modes-scope) says. Any number of questions can be asked, and they all run at the same time; asking another never stops or waits for one already running.
Each question's progress and results are shown in a [TaskTableScope](../../../ui/components/task-table/index.md#task-table-scope). The questions stack directly above the tabs, the newest nearest them, in a column that pushes the message list up to make room rather than covering it, so none of a running task's progress is ever hidden behind them. Each slides up out of the chat input with an animation as it is asked, the message list giving way above it. While the harness works on a question, it is a single row showing the latest thing the harness did. A finished question is a row with its status and first line.
However many questions are asked, the stack is only as tall as its rows, up to 240 pixels, the queue's most, and scrolls beyond that with a [ScrollbarScope](../../../ui/components/scrollbar/index.md#scrollbar-scope), kept on the newest question, nearest the tabs, as each is asked. Once it holds more than fit, the stack lays out only the rows in view, as a table does, so a long stack costs no more to show, scroll, or animate than a short one, and the drawer's bottom follows the stack's top as ever.
Once a question is complete, it opens onto a heading, with its status and first line, above its full task table, in the [AnswerDrawerScope](../answer-drawer/index.md#answer-drawer-scope), which it fills, the table scrolling once it is taller, with its lock to the bottom off to start with. Only one question is open at a time: opening another closes the one open back down to its row. An open question leaves the stack for the drawer. Clicking an open question's heading closes it down to its row in the stack, and clicking a finished question's row opens it again. Each question has a close button, which removes it and stops it if it is still running, leaving the others running. A closed question becomes a previous answer.

#### Answer Steps

For a question, only the answer matters, so wherever a finished question's task table is shown, an open question and a previous answer, the table collapses the steps leading up to the answer, as the [TaskTableScope](../../../ui/components/task-table/index.md#task-table-scope) says. A question closed into the previous answers starts collapsed again. Tasks are never collapsed like this: see the [MessageList](../message-list/index.md#message-list).

# Harness Integration Scope

## Concept

### Pitch

Uses the one-off version of a coding harness for the selected ProjectDirectoryScope: `claude -p`, `codex exec`, or `opencode run`, whichever the user chose. Each run carries on a conversation, so the harness keeps its context between requests.

### Shape

#### Description

Should always run in auto mode.
The compiled systemPrompt of a prompt's hidden anchor is appended to the harness's own system prompt, for example with `--append-system-prompt`.
The prompt is given to the harness on its standard input, and what the harness does is streamed back as it happens. A task's run takes its prompt as a stream of messages rather than a single one, so it can be fed more while it works, as its feeding says.
Its directory, which a system prompt's HARNESS_DIRECTORY stands for, is that of the harness in use: .claude, .codex, or .opencode.

#### Harnesses

The harness in use is the one picked in the [SettingsWindowScope](../settings-window/index.md#settings-window-scope): Claude Code, Codex, or OpenCode, Claude Code until another is picked. It is remembered for the user, as the [UserPreferencesScope](../user-preferences/index.md#user-preferences-scope) says, not for a project. Every run the application starts goes to it, the tasks, the questions, the palette's file search, the one-off runs, and the notes and commit messages it writes, and everything else works the same whichever it is. A run already going when another is picked finishes with the harness it started with, and a conversation is only carried on by the harness it began with; the next request with another harness starts a new one.
Each harness is run its own way, streaming what it does as a line of JSON per event, which is read into the same reply, tool calls, usage, and result, whichever harness wrote it:

- Claude Code is `claude -p`, in auto mode, the system prompt given with `--append-system-prompt`, a conversation carried on with `--resume`, and a copy of one with `--fork-session`.
- Codex is `codex exec`, with `--full-auto` and `--json`, the prompt read from its standard input, a conversation carried on with `resume`.
- OpenCode is `opencode run`, with `--format json`, a conversation carried on with `--session`.

Codex and OpenCode take no system prompt of their own, so it is given ahead of the prompt, marked off from it. Neither can carry on a copy of a conversation, so a question asked while another is running starts a new conversation with them instead. The notes and commit messages are written with a small model where the harness can be told one, Claude Code's haiku, and with the harness's default model otherwise.
When the harness picked isn't installed, a run fails saying that it can't be run, as any run that can't be started does.

#### Feeding

A task's run is given its prompt as a stream of messages: Claude Code with `--input-format stream-json`, each message written as a line of JSON on the harness's standard input, which stays open for as long as the run lasts. The run's first message is the task's compiled prompt, as ever, and each message sent to the task after it, from the [ChatInputScope](../prompt-mode/chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope), is written as another.
A message reaches the harness when it finishes what it is doing rather than interrupting it, so a run that is mid-tool-call takes it once that call is over. The harness echoes each message back as it takes it in, with `--replay-user-messages`. A message taken in between turns is answered with a result of its own, and one taken while a turn is under way is answered within that turn, sharing its result. A result no longer ends the task on its own: the run ends with a result once every message sent has been taken in, at which point its input is closed and the task finishes, in the state of that last result. A run that is stopped closes its input straight away.
Codex's `codex exec` and OpenCode's `opencode run` read a single prompt and can't be fed more while they work, so a task running with either takes its prompt as ever and can't be sent more.
Questions, the palette's file search, the one-off runs, and the notes and commit messages each take a single prompt, as ever.

#### Context

The harness keeps its context between requests instead of starting fresh each time. Tasks share one ongoing conversation, and each task sent carries it on. When the project is opened, tasks carry on the latest conversation in its history. Questions from the Ask tab share a separate conversation of their own, and when the project is opened they carry on the latest conversation among the questions saved with it. A question asked while another is running carries on a copy of that conversation, so questions running at the same time never write over each other. A conversation is only carried on in the project it began in, each open project keeping its own tasks' and questions' conversations while it is in the background, and if one can't be carried on, the next request starts a new one. Each run applies its own prompt's systemPrompt, even when it carries on a conversation begun in a different mode. The palette's file search always starts fresh.
A conversation can be left for a new one, from the chat input's New conversation button, as the [ChatInputScope](../prompt-mode/chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope) says: the next request starts a new conversation with no context, and the one left is not carried on again, not by a run of it still going, nor by the project's history. Leaving it is kept with the project, as the [ProjectDataScope](../project-data/index.md#project-data-scope) says, so a project opened after its tasks' or questions' conversation was left starts a new one too, rather than carrying on the latest conversation in its history, until a run after the reset begins one of its own. How much context a conversation holds is known from what the harness reports with each reply: everything the model was given, cached or not, and what it wrote, as of its latest reply; replies of subagents don't count.

# Usage Computation in TurnCompleted Event

The `usage` field is computed by calling `self.usage_from_last_total()`, which extracts data from the most recently updated total token usage:

**Code setting it:**
```rust
events.push(ThreadEvent::TurnCompleted(TurnCompletedEvent {
    usage: self.usage_from_last_total(),
}));
```

**Usage fields populated:**
The `Usage` struct contains:
- `input_tokens`
- `cached_input_tokens`
- `cache_write_input_tokens`
- `output_tokens`
- `reasoning_output_tokens`

**Scope:**
These values come from `"last_total_token_usage"` which is set whenever a `ThreadTokenUsageUpdated` notification arrives. The code accesses `"usage.total"` from that notification, indicating this represents **cumulative usage for the entire thread/session**, not just the current turn.
